test_title: PYST 22: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is known as the 'Steel City of India'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jamshedpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jamshedpur is popularly known as the **Steel City of India** due to its massive steel production and industrial infrastructure.
 
• It was founded by **Jamsetji Tata**, the founder of Tata Group, in 1907 and serves as the headquarters of Tata Steel, one of India's largest steel manufacturers.
 
• The city is located in the state of **Jharkhand** and is one of the first planned industrial cities in India.
 
• Jamshedpur is renowned for its clean environment, well-maintained infrastructure, and contributions to India's industrial sector.
 
• It houses one of the largest steel plants in India, contributing significantly to India's economy and employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steel Industry in India:**

 
 
• India is one of the largest producers of steel globally, with major contributions from cities like Jamshedpur, Rourkela, and Bhilai.
 
• The steel industry plays a crucial role in sectors like construction, automotive, and infrastructure.
 
• India's steel production is driven by companies like Tata Steel, Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), and JSW Steel.
 
 
 
• **Tata Steel:**
 
 
• Tata Steel is one of the world's leading steel producers, headquartered in Jamshedpur.
 
• Founded in 1907, it operates one of India's first integrated steel plants and has a global footprint.
 
• The company emphasizes sustainability and innovation in steel production.
 
 
 
• **Planned Cities in India:**
 
 
• Jamshedpur is one of India's earliest planned cities, designed with a focus on industrial growth and urban development.
 
• Other notable planned cities include Chandigarh and Navi Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Jamsetji Tata:**
 
 
• Jamsetji Tata is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Industry" for his contributions to industrial growth in India.
 
• He envisioned Jamshedpur as a hub for steel production and a model industrial city.
 
• His legacy continues through the Tata Group's initiatives in various sectors.
